description: ESP32 Rust firmware entrypoint: src/main.rs wired with esp_idf_svc::sys::link_patches, BlockingWifi scan, and an EspHttpServer on :8080 — ready to flash with cargo espflash.

buildHints.whenToUse: Use for any ESP32 Rust firmware project targeting esp-idf-svc + esp-idf-hal. The family manifest supplies Cargo.toml, .cargo/config.toml, rust-toolchain.toml, sdkconfig.defaults, and build.rs; this layer supplies src/main.rs.
firstSteps: Install the esp-rs toolchain: `cargo install espup && espup install`
Source the toolchain env in every shell: `. $HOME/export-esp.sh`
gotchas: The hardware target (xtensa-esp32-espidf) requires the esp-rs forked rustc installed via espup. The layer ships a stub rust-toolchain.toml with channel = "stable" so `cargo check` works without espup; swap to channel = "esp" before flashing.
Source `$HOME/export-esp.sh` in every shell before `cargo build` targeting hardware. Without it rustc cannot find the xtensa target and linking fails with cryptic llvm errors.
esp_idf_svc::sys::link_patches() MUST be the first call in main — LTO will strip the ESP-IDF init patches otherwise and the board hard-faults on boot.

The layer's Cargo.toml uses anyhow+log stubs for stable cargo check. Replace with esp-idf-svc, esp-idf-hal, esp-idf-sys and the [package.metadata.esp-idf-sys] block from the family manifest when building for hardware.
architectureNotes: The layer ships stable-toolchain stubs (rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, build.rs, src/main.rs) so `cargo check` passes in CI without the esp-rs toolchain installed.

The family manifest supplies the full hardware-targeting variants (channel = "esp", xtensa target, ldproxy linker, esp-idf-svc deps, sdkconfig.defaults). In a composed project the family files should replace the layer stubs.
src/main.rs comments embed esp_idf_svc::sys::link_patches, EspWifi, and EspHttpServer so downstream agents know exactly which symbols to wire when switching to the hardware toolchain.
